name: Menu Button
description: A button that opens a menu, typically styled with a downward-pointing arrow to indicate that activation will display a list of menu choices.

keyboard_interactions.action: Opens the menu and places focus on the first menu item
Opens the menu and places focus on the first menu item
Opens the menu and focuses the first item
Opens the menu and focuses the last item
Moves focus to next item; wraps from last to first
Moves focus to previous item; wraps from first to last
Moves focus to first / last item
Closes the menu and returns focus to the button
Closes the menu and moves focus onward — must never be trapped

required_attributes.description: State. On the BUTTON, never on the menu.
Menu items are NOT links or buttons. Inside role='menu', only menuitem roles are valid children.
Roving tabindex: items are focused programmatically with .focus(), never by Tab. Unlike combobox, real DOM focus DOES move here.

notes: Menu items follow the menu/menubar pattern for keyboard interaction
When the menu closes, focus returns to the button
role='menu' is for ACTIONS (Edit, Duplicate, Delete) — the desktop-application menu pattern. It is NOT for site navigation.
A nav bar of links is not a menu: use <nav> + <ul> + <a>. Adding role='menu' to it makes screen readers announce a menu and demand arrow keys that links do not provide.
A show/hide of arbitrary content is a disclosure, not a menu — see patterns/disclosure.md.
Unlike combobox, this pattern uses REAL focus: call .focus() on the item. Do not use aria-activedescendant here.
role='menu' children must be menuitem/menuitemradio/menuitemcheckbox. Putting <a href> or <button> inside role='menu' produces invalid, inconsistently-announced markup.
native_element: none — but most 'menus' are not menus. See the decision table in patterns/menu-button.md.

raweb_criteria.reason: aria-haspopup and aria-expanded must be exposed so the button announces that it opens a menu, and whether it is open.
Enter/Space/Down must open the menu; arrows must move between items; Escape must close and restore focus.
The focused menu item must be visibly indicated — real focus moves here, unlike combobox.
A closed menu must be hidden from assistive technologies, not just visually.
Focus moves to the first item on open and returns to the button on close, keeping the sequence coherent.
Escape and Tab must always let the keyboard user out of the menu.
